# Intake Brief — When ships explode when a level times out we need major SFX explosion (AH-0MUJ1YZJ9008O4RC)

> **Status of this brief:** context gathered; three product decisions are
> unresolved (see Appendix). This provisional brief documents the evidence
> and assumptions and is flagged `needsProducerReview`. The stage remains
> `idea`; intake is finalised once the questions are answered.

## Problem statement

When a wave times out, every surviving non-asteroid enemy detonates at 10×
scale (`WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE`), but no explosion sound plays for those
detonations. The only audio on the timeout path is the generic player
life-loss cue (`playDestructionSound()` via `_loseLife(false)`), so the
dramatic 10× visual blast lands silently.

## Users

- **Player** — the wave-timeout wipe should be audible as a major explosion,
  making the lost life and the 10× detonation feel consequential.
- **Developer / designer tuning feel** — one place (exported constants) to tune
  the cue's layering, volume and duration.

### Example user story

- As a **player**, when the level timer hits zero and my remaining enemies
  detonate, I hear a large, heavy explosion cue so the moment reads as a major
  event rather than a silent animation.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_timeoutWave()` detonates every non-asteroid
  survivor via `s.entity.destroySelf(WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE)` and calls
  `_loseLife(false)`; no SFX is triggered for the detonations.
  `WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE = 10`.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — `destroySelf(scale)` → `playExplosion(scale)`
  only spawns particles; the class comment states audio is played by the scene
  at destruction time.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playDestructionSound()` (generic 440→60 Hz
  sawtooth pop) and the layered `playPlayerDestructionSound()` (impact thump +
  descending body + noise tail). No "major" or timeout-specific cue exists.
- GDD §7.3 documents the two existing cues and states "the wave-timeout life
  penalty and shield absorption keep the generic cue".
- Tests live in `src/audio/effects.test.ts`, `src/audio/effectsMaster.test.ts`
  and `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`.

## Desired change

Add a major explosion SFX that plays when ships detonate on level/wave
timeout, wired into `PlayScene._timeoutWave()` (and any shared timeout path
that may exist), with exported tuning constants, GDD §7.3 documentation, and
automated tests.

## Assumptions (to validate)

1. The cue fires **once per timeout event**, not once per detonating ship. [ASSUMPTION]
2. It is a **new dedicated procedural cue** (not a re-use of
   `playPlayerDestructionSound()`), so it can be tuned independently. [ASSUMPTION]
3. It routes through the existing SFX master gain/mute plumbing and is a safe
   no-op without an `AudioContext`. [ASSUMPTION]
4. Scope is **audio only** — the 10× particle blast already exists, so no new
   VFX. [ASSUMPTION]
5. It applies to the game's `PlayScene` timeout; gym scenes have no wave
   timeout unless one is added. [ASSUMPTION]

## Tentative Acceptance Criteria (provisional — pending answers)

1. A dedicated major-explosion cue is defined in `src/audio/effects.ts` with
   all amplitudes/durations as exported constants and documented in GDD §7.3.
2. When a wave/level times out with surviving enemies, the cue plays exactly
   once (not once per ship) — verified by a `PlayScene` test.
3. When a wave/level times out with no enemies remaining, no explosion cue
   plays (existing AC3 behaviour preserved) — verified by test.
4. The cue routes through the SFX master volume/mute and is a safe no-op
   without an `AudioContext` — verified by test.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> ACs 1–4 are provisional pending the open questions below.

## Related work

- AH-0MU7JTG9R002ZWA6 — Wave time limit: surviving enemies detonate at 10x
  scale and cost a life (added the timeout detonation; completed).
- AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L — Asteroids should not explode when time runs out,
  instead carry them over (completed).
- AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZY — Need juice when the player is destroyed (precedent for
  a dedicated layered cue; completed).
- AH-0MUDY2ID7006VY3A — dedicated player-destruction cue (implemented
  `playPlayerDestructionSound`).
- AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V — Add particle-based explosion VFX for enemy and player
  deaths (completed).
- AH-0MU0AVBWH002ZWRH — Add randomness to explosion (completed).
- AH-0MUA8B6MT006M1KS — SFX master volume + mute plumbing in effects.ts
  (completed).
- AH-0MUA8BEUR006RWCI — SettingsScene: SFX volume slider + mute toggle
  (completed).
- AH-0MU3VPIA900697E8 — Ensure all enemies have SFX on their fire event
  (completed).
- AH-0MT7UW0Y80062NU1 — Bring simple audio effects into MVP scope in GDD
  (completed).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Blast granularity:** Should the "major SFX explosion" be one cue per
  timeout event, or one cue per detonating ship? — **OPEN QUESTION** (routed to
  producer). Recommended: A) one cue per timeout event.
  - A) A single cue fired once per timeout (recommended) — avoids N heavy cues
    stacking/clipping in the same frame.
  - B) One heavy cue per detonating ship (needs attenuation/rate-limiting).
  - C) A single cue plus a short per-ship tail.
- **Q2 — Cue identity:** Should this be a new dedicated cue or a reuse of an
  existing one? — **OPEN QUESTION** (routed to producer). Recommended: A) new
  dedicated layered cue.
  - A) New dedicated `playMajorExplosionSound()` (impact thump + descending
    body + noise tail), deeper/longer than and distinct from
    `playDestructionSound()` (recommended).
  - B) Reuse `playPlayerDestructionSound()`.
  - C) Boost `playDestructionSound()` for this path only.
- **Q3 — Player life-loss cue on timeout:** Should the player's timeout life
  loss also be upgraded to the heavy player-destruction cue, or do only the
  enemy detonations get the major SFX? — **OPEN QUESTION** (routed to
  producer). Recommended: A) keep the generic player life-loss cue.
  - A) Keep the generic player life-loss cue and add only the blast cue
    (recommended).
  - B) Also play `playPlayerDestructionSound()` for the timeout life loss.
  - C) Both.

Options: (a) start from all static `LEVELS`, override the configured levels per their source, and append generated levels numbered beyond `LEVEL_COUNT`; (b) the campaign is exactly the configured levels, with scripted ones referencing `LEVELS` by number; (c) all static levels are scripted by default and only configured levels are generated.

**Recommended:** (a) start from all static `LEVELS` — preserves the shipped five-level campaign and guarantees onboarding levels exist.

This is blocking: it determines which levels exist in a mixed campaign and their order. Recorded in the intake draft Appendix as OPEN QUESTION.

question: What is the fallback scope when a generated level has no usable curve, or the candidate pool is empty? Options: (a) per-level — use that level's static `LEVELS` definition if one exists, otherwise apply a safe guard; (b) whole-campaign — fall back to all of static `LEVELS` (current builder behaviour); (c) per-level for a bad level, whole-campaign only when the entire config is empty.

**Recommended:** (a) per-level fallback — one bad level must not discard the rest of a mixed campaign.

This is blocking: it determines the fallback ACs and test matrix. Recorded in the intake draft Appendix as OPEN QUESTION.

question: Intake needs producer input on three decisions before the ACs can be finalised (full context and provisional brief in the description).

Q1 (blast granularity) — Should the major explosion SFX be one cue per timeout event, or one cue per detonating ship? Recommended: A) a single cue fired once per timeout, because a wave can contain 10+ survivors and playing a heavy cue per ship in the same frame risks clipping/cacophony. Options: A) single cue per timeout (recommended); B) one heavy cue per detonating ship (needs attenuation/rate-limiting); C) single cue plus a short per-ship tail.

Q2 (cue identity) — Should this be a new dedicated cue or a re-use of an existing one? Recommended: A) a new dedicated `playMajorExplosionSound()` (impact thump + descending body + noise tail), deeper/longer than and distinct from `playDestructionSound()`. Options: A) new dedicated cue (recommended); B) reuse `playPlayerDestructionSound()`; C) boost `playDestructionSound()` for this path only.

Q3 (player life-loss cue on timeout) — Should the player's timeout life loss also be upgraded to the heavy player-destruction cue, or do only the enemy detonations get the major SFX? Recommended: A) keep the generic player life-loss cue and add only the blast cue. Options: A) keep generic player cue (recommended); B) also play `playPlayerDestructionSound()` on the timeout life loss; C) both.

Context: `PlayScene._timeoutWave()` detonates every non-asteroid survivor at 10x scale but plays no SFX for those detonations; the only audio is the generic `playDestructionSound()` via `_loseLife(false)`. Precedent for a dedicated layered cue: AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZY / AH-0MUDY2ID7006VY3A. Intake stage left at idea; flagged needsProducerReview.
